sections.heading: A Watch Box Is Judged by How the Watch Sits in It
sections.text: Fit Before Finish A Watch Box Is Judged by How the Watch Sits in It Everything else on a watch box — the foil, the wrap, the closure — is decided after one thing is right: whether the timepiece sits square, snug and centred when the lid opens. A watch that lolls to one side on an oversized pillow undoes an otherwise expensive box in the first second of the reveal. That fit is not a craftsmanship intangible. It comes from three measurements and one decision, and getting them onto the dieline early is what separates a sample that is approved from one that goes round twice. Compare with our magnetic rigid box or the lid-and-base format with ribbon if your programme covers more than watches.

sections.heading: The Three Measurements That Decide the Cushion
sections.text: Cushion Engineering The Three Measurements That Decide the Cushion Send us these three numbers with your enquiry and we can cut a cushion that fits at first sample instead of third. Case diameter. Men's dress and sports watches commonly land between 38 mm and 44 mm; women's pieces frequently run 28 mm to 36 mm. This sets how much lateral room the pillow needs so the case does not touch the side walls. Case thickness, measured over the crystal. This is the one that gets forgotten. A dive watch or an automatic with a domed sapphire crystal can be materially taller than its spec sheet suggests, and a lid toleranced to a flat dress watch will press on the glass. Measure the tallest point, not the case band. Strap or bracelet type. A steel bracelet holds a wider, rounder loop than a leather strap of the same nominal length, so the two need different pillow circumferences. A pillow cut for leather will splay a bracelet; one cut for a bracelet leaves a leather strap slack. Worked example. A 42 mm sports watch, 13 mm thick over a slightly domed crystal, on a steel bracelet. The pillow needs a circumference that holds the bracelet without forcing the clasp open, and the interior height must clear 13 mm plus the pillow's own compressed height — not 13 mm flat. Specify the box interior to the compressed stack, and the lid closes without pressure on the crystal. Specify it to the case alone and you get a lid that appears to shut but bears on the glass every time it is closed. If your range spans widely — say a 34 mm dress model alongside a 44 mm chronograph — one cushion rarely serves both well. A pillow sized to the larger case will physically hold the smaller one, but it will look lost in it. Two cushion sizes inside one shared outer box is usually the better answer, and it keeps a single outer tooling across the range.

sections.heading: Presentation Box or Shipper? They Are Not the Same Box
sections.text: Protection In Transit Presentation Box or Shipper? They Are Not the Same Box A recurring and expensive assumption is that the presentation box can double as the shipping carton. It rarely can, and watches are unforgiving about it. A presentation box is engineered for the reveal: it opens easily, it holds the piece in a soft cushion, and it is finished on the outside because the customer sees it. A shipper is engineered for compression, drop and vibration. Ship a rigid presentation box on its own and two things happen — the corners crush and arrive dented, and the watch works loose in a cushion that was designed to be opened gently, not shaken for days. Retail and boutique — presentation box inside a plain outer shipper, with void fill. The presentation box arrives pristine because it never touched the courier. Direct-to-consumer — presentation box inside a branded mailer sized to it. This is where the unboxing sequence is worth designing: the mailer is the first impression, the presentation box the second. Gifting and events — presentation box with a fitted sleeve or outer rigid box, which also solves the problem of a customer carrying it without a bag. The practical test on your sample: close the box, hold it shut, and invert it. If the watch shifts in the cushion when the box is upside down, it will shift in a courier van. Tighten the cushion, do not add tape.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.text: Frequently Asked Frequently Asked Questions What is the MOQ for custom watch boxes? 100 pcs for rigid and magnetic watch boxes. A custom cushion tool for an unusual case size may carry its own minimum, which we confirm on the quote rather than after the order. How do you size the cushion to our watch? From three numbers: case diameter, case thickness measured over the crystal, and strap type. Send the watch or those three measurements and we cut to suit — a bracelet and a leather strap need different pillow circumferences. Can one box fit several models in our range? Often yes. A cushion sized to your largest case will hold smaller ones, but a small watch looks lost on an oversized pillow. Where a range spans widely we usually recommend two cushion sizes sharing one outer box, which keeps a single outer tooling. How long does production take? Bulk production runs 12 to 15 working days after sample approval. A physical pre-production sample takes 3 to 5 days. Can the box carry our logo? Yes — foil stamping, embossing, debossing and spot UV on the outer wrap, and the interior lining can carry a printed or debossed mark as well. Do you supply watch boxes wholesale to retailers and distributors? Yes. Watch boxes are made to order at the Shenzhen factory and supplied wholesale from 100 pcs per design for rigid and magnetic styles. When one order covers models with very different case sizes, two cushion sizes can share one outer box, so the wholesale order keeps a single outer tooling.
